learn.title: What is a rate?
learn.body: A rate compares two quantities with different units, such as miles and hours, or dollars and kilograms. If a car travels 150 miles in 3 hours, the rate is 150 miles per 3 hours.

learn.title: The unit rate
learn.body: A unit rate has 1 in the denominator. Divide to find it: $150\div 3=50$ miles per hour. This is the speed. The word per means divided by, so miles per hour is miles $\div$ hours.

learn.title: Which is the better buy?
learn.body: A small jar has 12 ounces for 3 dollars. A large jar has 20 ounces for 4.20 dollars.
steps: The large jar costs less per ounce, so it is the better buy.

learn.title: Using a unit rate
learn.body: Once you know the unit rate, finding any amount is a single multiplication. At 50 miles per hour, 2.5 hours covers $50\times 2.5=125$ miles. To find the time for a distance, divide the distance by the rate.
Always compare unit rates when you compare prices. Put the same unit on the bottom for both items.

questions.prompt: A car drives 150 miles in 3 hours. What is its speed?
Typing 240 words in 6 minutes is how many words per minute?
A rate of 4 dollars for 8 apples is \_\_ dollars per apple.

questions.explanation: The large jar costs 0.21 dollars per ounce and the small jar costs 0.25 dollars per ounce.

questions.prompt: At 90 miles per hour, how many miles in 2.5 hours?
questions.explanation: Multiply the rate by the time: $90\times 2.5=225$.

questions.prompt: A tap fills 48 litres in 16 minutes. How many litres per minute?
Match each situation with its unit rate.
questions.explanation: Divide the first amount by the second: $60\div 2=30$, $10\div 4=2.5$, $200\div 5=40$.
